arxiv-2011-07997.title: Comparative Probing of Lexical Semantics Theories for Cognitive Plausibility and Technological Usefulness
arxiv-2011-07997.creator: University of Lisbon NLX GroupFaculdade de CiênciasLisbon, Portugal, António Branco, João Rodrigues, Małgorzata Salawa, Ruben Branco, Chakaveh Saedi
arxiv-2011-07997.description: Abstract Lexical semantics theories differ in advocating that the meaning of words is represented as an inference graph, a feature mapping or a vector space, thus raising the question: is it the case that one of these approaches is superior to the others in representing lexical semantics appropriately?

arxiv-2012-15764.title: Divergence Regulated Encoder Network for Joint Dimensionality Reduction and Classification
arxiv-2012-15764.creator: Joshua Peeples, Sarah Walker, Connor McCurley, Alina Zare, James Keller, and Weihuang Xu
arxiv-2012-15764.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Joshua Peeples, Sarah Walker, Connor McCurley, Alina Zare, James Keller, and Weihuang Xu. Feature representation is an important aspect of remote-sensing based image classification. While deep convolutional neural networks are able to effectively amalgamate information, large numbers of parameters often make learned features inscrutable and difficult to transfer to alternative models. In order to better represent statistical texture information for remote-sensing image classification, in this paper, we investigate performing joint dimensionality reduction and classification using a novel histogram neural network.

arxiv-2110-07351.title: Shortened Polarization Kernels
arxiv-2110-07351.creator: Grigorii Trofimiuk
arxiv-2110-07351.description: Abstract A shortening method for large polarization kernels is presented, which results in shortened kernels with the highest error exponent if applied to kernels of size up to 32. It uses lower and upper bounds on partial distances for quick elimination of unsuitable shortening patterns.

arxiv-2110-08277.title: Kink-antikink scattering in a quantum vacuum
arxiv-2110-08277.creator: Mainak Mukhopadhyay, Evangelos I. Sfakianakis, Tanmay Vachaspati, and George Zahariade
arxiv-2110-08277.description: Abstract We study kink-antikink scattering in the sine-Gordon model in the presence of interactions with an additional scalar field, ψ \psi , that is in its quantum vacuum. In contrast to the classical scattering, now there is quantum radiation of ψ \psi quanta and the kink-antikink may form bound states that resemble breathers of the sine-Gordon model.

arxiv-2312-04758.title: Physics-Informed Convolutional Autoencoder for Cyber Anomaly Detection in Power Distribution Grids
arxiv-2312-04758.creator: Mehdi Jabbari Zideh, , Sarika Khushalani Solanki
arxiv-2312-04758.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Mehdi Jabbari Zideh, , Sarika Khushalani Solanki. The growing trend toward the modernization of power distribution systems has facilitated the installation of advanced measurement units and promotion of the cyber communication systems. However, these infrastructures are still prone to stealth cyber attacks. The existing data-driven anomaly detection methods suffer from a lack of knowledge about the system’s physics, lack of interpretability, and scalability issues hindering their practical applications in real-world scenarios. To address these concerns, physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) were introduced.

arxiv-2411-01195.title: Transfer Learning for Finetuning Large Language Models
arxiv-2411-01195.creator: Tobias Strangmann, Lennart Purucker, Jörg K.H. Franke, Ivo Rapant, Fabio Ferreira, Frank Hutter
arxiv-2411-01195.description: Abstract As the landscape of large language models expands, efficiently finetuning for specific tasks becomes increasingly crucial. At the same time, the landscape of parameter-efficient finetuning methods rapidly expands. Consequently, practitioners face a multitude of complex choices when searching for an optimal finetuning pipeline for large language models.

arxiv-2510-26220.creator: J. Philidet, K. Belkacem

pmc-10665658.title: A revisit to the specification of sub-datasets and corresponding coverage timespans when using Web of Science Core Collection
pmc-10665658.creator: Andy Wai Kan Yeung
pmc-10665658.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Many papers used the Web of Science Core Collection (WOSCC) as the data source. The work by Liu (2019, Scientometrics) revealed that only 48 % of such papers published in information science and library science journals during 2017–2018 specified which sub-datasets they used, and subsequently urged researchers to provide such information together with the corresponding coverage timespans to improve transparency and reproducibility. This work revisited this issue to reveal if the current condition has improved following Liu's recommendations.

pmc-11536148.creator: Liyao Qin, Huifeng Yue, Zhihua Gong, Yuqiong Guo, Dan Li, Li Ma, Zhuoma YiXi, Jing He, Zhihong Li, Guangke Li, Wei Yan, Nan Sang
pmc-11536148.description: SignificanceEpidemiological studies suggest a link between air pollution and adverse birth outcomes, though these findings are controversial. This study integrates the retrospective epidemiological analysis with toxicological experiments to confirm the causal relationship between maternal nitrogen dioxide (NO2) exposure and an increased risk of fetal growth restriction (FGR).

pmc-11714656.title: Physical exercise prevents age‐related changes in [11C]PK11195 uptake in a mouse model of Down Syndrome
pmc-11714656.creator: Chiara Maria Righini, Larissa Estessi de Souza, Jean Marques Brizola, Lidia Emmanuela Wiazowski Spelta, Daniele de Paula de Paula Faria
pmc-11714656.description: BackgroundDown syndrome (DS) is associated with mitochondrial dysfunction leading to higher levels of oxidative stress and cell degeneration. This fact, together with the overexpression of AD‐related genes in trisomy 21, increases the risk of developing Alzheimer's disease (AD). Thus, it is important to look for interventions that could prevent mitochondrial damage before symptoms occur.

pmc-12466651.title: Cyberviolence Against Women and Girls in Spanish Adolescents: Experiences of Cyberaggression and Cybervictimization
pmc-12466651.creator: Virginia Ferreiro Basurto, Esperanza Bosch Fiol, Maria Antonia Manassero Mas, Victoria A Ferrer-Pérez, Phillip Ozimek
pmc-12466651.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Understanding the scope of cyberviolence against women and girls in adolescents and the differences between girls and boys is a fundamental starting point for its prevention. This study analyzes the experiences of cyberaggression and cybervictimization perpetrated and suffered by 762 adolescents (399 girls and 363 boys) aged 14 and 15 in the Balearic Islands (Spain) through a diagnostic study of an electronic survey administering the Gender Violence 2.0 questionnaire.

pmc-12522313.title: Factors influencing delayed medical treatment in children with retinoblastoma: a qualitative study
pmc-12522313.creator: Hong Ji, Junzhao Chen, Na Du, Shanshan Xiong, Yinghui Wu, Changjuan Zeng
pmc-12522313.description: BackgroundRetinoblastoma (RB) is the most common primary intraocular malignancy in children. Its 5-year survival rate exceeds 90% if diagnosed early. However, delayed care-seeking allows the disease to advance to late stages and can become life-threatening. This study employed qualitative methods to characterise the experiences underlying delayed presentation among children with RB.

The doses required for complete protein removal and stabilization were determined and then applied to clarify a Malvazija istarska (Vitis vinifera L.

We aim to compare the clinical outcomes of P/T treatment in two models of OPAT care in order to maximize the utilization of health resources.

pmc-13029202.title: Optimization of Thyme, Cinnamon, and Black Seed Oil Combinations for Enhanced Antibacterial and Antioxidant Efficacy: Mixture Design and In Silico Insights
pmc-13029202.creator: Mahmoud S. Maher, Dina A. Altwiley, Dalal M. Alkuraythi, Mahmoud M. A. Moustafa, Mary S. Khalil, Tarek A. A. Moussa, Nawal Magdy

While several studies have investigated individual oils and binary combinations, fewer reports have examined ternary mixtures using systematic optimization approaches.

pmc-13215489.creator: Zhiyuan Gao, Jiaolei Zhang, Lei Cao
pmc-13215489.description: Steel plates and bolted connections have become common construction details in prefabricated structural systems. However, prefabricated frame structures with steel plate hoop–bolted connections exhibit connection gaps, interface slip, and discontinuous force-transfer paths, making them prone to hysteretic degradation and cumulative damage under seismic loading.

pmc-13416406.title: Nanomaterial-Enhanced Corneal Cross-Linking: Engineering Strategies for Transforming Keratoconus Management
pmc-13416406.creator: Liqin Huang, Yao Fu, Fang Li
pmc-13416406.description: Keratoconus, a progressive corneal ectasia, remains a major cause of irreversible visual impairment worldwide. Conventional corneal cross-linking (CXL) with riboflavin/ultraviolet A (UVA) has revolutionized clinical management, yet its efficacy is still constrained by epithelial barriers, oxygen dependence, and safety concerns in thin corneas. Emerging nanotechnology provides a transformative opportunity to overcome these bottlenecks.

pmc-13540385.creator: Yu‐Hua Chen, Chung‐Liang Li, Ping‐Fu Yang, Hui‐Hua Hsiao, Fang‐Ming Chen, Sin‐Hua Moi
pmc-13540385.description: Preoperative diagnosis of ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) may be followed by pathological upstaging to invasive ductal carcinoma (IDC) upon surgical excision, a discrepancy that significantly impacts surgical planning and decisions regarding sentinel lymph node biopsy (SLNB). This retrospective study aimed to evaluate clinical indicators associated with such upstaging and develop a nomogram‐based clinical estimation model for risk stratification.
